chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Hamzah who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'If a man marries a mature woman (thayyib) who has been married to another husband, and she claims that he has not had intercourse with her since he entered into marriage with her, then the word in this matter is the word of the husband, and he must swear by Allah that he has indeed had intercourse with her, because she is the claimant.'

He said: 'If he married her while she was a virgin (bakr) and she claimed that he had not reached her, then this is something known by women, so let a trustworthy woman among them look at her. If she says that she is a virgin, then it is upon the Imam to delay him for a year. If he had intercourse with her, then [the claim is rejected]; otherwise, they are separated, and she is given half of the dowry, and there is no waiting period (iddah) upon her.'

key_terms.اَلثَّيِّب: A mature woman who has been previously married
key_terms.اَلْعِدَّة: The waiting period for a woman after divorce or death of husband

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on proving consummation of marriage when a wife claims non-consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the jurisprudential distinction in marital disputes based on the wife's prior marital status, reflecting the Shia emphasis on evidentiary standards in family law. For a previously married woman (*thayyib*), the husband's oath is sufficient due to the presumption of consummation, whereas for a virgin (*bakr*), the claim requires verification by a trustworthy female witness, potentially leading to a one-year period of *tadlis* (delay) before divorce if consummation is not proven. This ruling underscores the practical application of *qasamah* (oath-taking) and *shahada* (testimony) in resolving *khula* or *faskh* scenarios within the Imami tradition.
